# A guidance to TK1104 {.unnumbered}

This script accompanies the course **TK1104 Digital Technology**. Each
chapter belongs to one lecture: Chapter 1 to Lecture 1, Chapter 2 to
Lecture 2, and so on, and each is followed in the same week by its guided
Practice session. The slides shown in the lectures carry the same
structure, so slides, script and exercises can be used side by side.

In this course, the lectures themselves are the curriculum — the exam will
not ask for book-only material. The script therefore does something simple
but useful: It re-tells each lecture in connected prose, slowly enough to
be read, so that you can prepare a lecture before it happens and
reconstruct it afterwards without deciphering bullet points. The
recommended textbook — Fox, *Information Technology*, 2nd edition — adds
depth where you want it; the short per-lecture reading (15–30 minutes) is
listed in `Readings.xlsx` on Canvas.

Scattered through the chapters you will find a few grey boxes headed
*Excursus*. They draw on textbooks that generations of computer-science
students grew up with — Tanenbaum and Austin's *Structured Computer
Organization*, Tanenbaum and Bos's *Modern Operating Systems*, and, for
the networking chapters, Dostálek and Kabelová's *Understanding TCP/IP* —
and they supply background, history and the occasional deeper "why"
behind something the lecture states. Read them for perspective and
enjoyment: They are **not** exam material, and skipping them costs you
nothing on the multiple-choice paper. The blue boxes headed *Worked
exercise* are the opposite: Small worked tasks — convert this, encode
that, build this gate — placed right next to the technique they practise,
each with its compact solution. Do them with the solution covered; they
are the stepping stones to each chapter's self-check, and the self-checks
are the stepping stones to the exam.

Lecture 12 (exam preparation) is delivered live in the final session and
has no chapter of its own in this script; Chapter 11 closes the written
part.

A practical suggestion from someone who once learned from a script very
much like this one: Read a chapter with a pen. Mark what is obvious, mark
what is not, and bring the second list to the lecture. That is the
cheapest exam preparation you will ever do.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading in the dark

Every page of this script has a dark mode: Use the toggle in the
navigation bar to switch between the light and the dark theme. The
setting is remembered as you move between chapters.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Annotate this script

You can highlight and annotate any passage of this script with Hypothesis
— select text and comment directly in the margin (a free account at
[hypothes.is](https://hypothes.is) is needed).
:::
